Businesses using AI are far more optimistic about their growth:

Among US firms using AI, the share expecting revenue to increase over the next 12 months exceeds the share expecting a decrease by 48.2 percentage points, according to the Federal Reserve Banks' 2025 Small Business Credit Survey.

By comparison, this gap is just 20.6 percentage points among firms not using AI, less than half the figure for AI adopters.

At the same time, the share of AI-using firms expecting employment to increase exceeds the share expecting a decrease by 32.7 percentage points, compared to just 15.2 percentage points among non-adopters.

These differences persist even after accounting for firm characteristics, business-owner demographics, and changes in revenue and employment over the previous 12 months.

After adjusting for these factors, the gap between firms expecting revenue growth and those expecting a decline remains 14 percentage points wider among AI adopters than non-adopters.

For employment expectations, the corresponding gap remains 10 percentage points wider among AI adopters.

Businesses using AI are significantly more optimistic about their future expansion.

Energy stocks are making history:

The S&P 500 Energy sector took just 196 trading days to gain +50% year-to-date, marking the 5th-fastest time any S&P 500 sector has reached this milestone since 1990.

For perspective, in 2022, the Energy sector surged +50% in just 94 trading days, the fastest pace recorded over the last 36 years.

By comparison, the Technology sector reached the same milestone in 133 and 160 trading days in 1996 and 1997, respectively.

Consumer Discretionary, Consumer Staples, Industrials, Materials, and Real Estate have never recorded a +50% annual gain since 1990.

The Energy sector is witnessing one of its most remarkable rallies in decades.

China's automotive industry is facing a historic slowdown:

China’s automotive industry profit margin fell to 3.6% in the first 8 months of 2026, its lowest in at least 12 years.

This is now on track for its 12th consecutive annual decline.

Years of heavy investment have created severe production overcapacity, while weakening domestic demand is intensifying price wars among car manufacturers.

Meanwhile, in the first 8 months of 2026, domestic passenger vehicle sales dropped -22% YoY.

For the full year, car sales are expected to fall -22% YoY, to 18.5 million, their lowest annual total since 2014.

Now, factories have the capacity to produce a record ~62.9 million vehicles this year, more than 3 times the expected sales figure.

China’s auto industry is struggling.

The AI revolution is leaving younger tech workers behind:

US software developer employment among workers aged 22-25 has fallen -20% since November 2022, when ChatGPT was launched.

Over the same period, the 26-30 age group has recorded a -4% decline.

By comparison, employment among developers aged 41-49 has surged +20%.

The 35-40 and 31-34 cohorts have grown +11% and +6%, respectively.

As a result, the employment growth gap between the youngest and the oldest group has risen to 40 percentage points.

The AI boom is destroying job opportunities for entry-level tech workers.

BREAKING: US existing home sales dropped -5.5% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 3.75 million, the lowest since August 2010.

Excluding the 2010 decline, this marks the lowest level since 1995.

YoY, existing home sales fell -8.8%, the largest annual decline since November 2023.

In the West, sales plunged -9.7% MoM last month, to an annualized rate of 650,000, the lowest since 1999.

Meanwhile, existing single-family home sales fell -5.8% MoM in October, to an annualized rate of 3.41 million, the lowest since October 2010.

This comes as 30Y mortgage rates surged to 7.6% last month, their highest level since 2000, excluding one month in 2023.

US housing demand is collapsing.

US inflation is diverging from the Fed’s target:

US CPI Inflation has surged +30.2% since January 2020, to an all-time high.

This translates into an annualized inflation rate of +4.0% over this period.

Meanwhile, under a steady 2% annual inflation target, cumulative CPI growth would have been just +14.3%.

In other words, actual cumulative inflation is +15.9 percentage points above the target path, more than double the implied increase.

This comes as CPI has remained above 2% for 67 consecutive months.

The gap began widening again in March, as inflation has now remained above 3% for 7 consecutive months.

On the Nvidia situation:

Nvidia's board can still make things right.

It has now been 48 hours since Jensen Huang resigned from his role as CEO, President, and board member of Nvidia.

Meanwhile, a thorough investigation has not been completed, countless critical questions are unanswered, and one of the world's greatest CEOs was forced out before the full facts of the situation were established.

In fact, the US Attorney General, the CIA, the DNI, and members of the House Intelligence Committee have also suggested that the current evidence remains inconclusive regarding whether Jensen Huang was involved in an affair with a Chinese spy.

The reality is that Jensen Huang resigned in the heat of the moment and the board acted based on speculative information.

We believe Nvidia's board, $NVDA, has a duty to shareholders to openly acknowledge that Jensen Huang could return to the company, pending a thorough investigation.

What happens in a CEO's personal life should not automatically dictate his role in a company, particularly if an investigation fails to establish national security misconduct or other wrongdoing that warrants removal.

The right move is to acknowledge that Jensen Huang is innocent until proven guilty.

Nvidia's board must do this now. It is not too late.
